title: Hancock Whitney Bank Appoints 28-Year Banking Veteran as Senior Vice President, Commercial Banking
summary: Hancock Whitney Bank welcomes Flowood-area banker Grant Rosenbaum as senior vice president, commercial banking.
body_markdown:
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
**Arian Pierre**
PR & Social Media Producer


arian.pierre@hancockwhitney.com
504-380-6257


**GULFPORT, Miss. October 20, 2026** — Hancock Whitney Bank — one of America’s strongest, safest banks — welcomes Flowood-area banker Grant Rosenbaum as senior vice president, commercial banking.


Rosenbaum has more than 28 years of banking experience and will be responsible for driving commercial lending growth and advancing Hancock Whitney's commitment to relationship-focused service and long-term investment in the communities the bank serves.


"Strong relationships are built through trust, expertise, and a commitment to understanding our clients' needs," said Hancock Whitney Bank Mississippi Regional President Leigh Pace. "Grant's extensive banking experience, leadership capabilities, and dedication to client success make him a tremendous addition to our team."


Known for a relationship-focused approach, Rosenbaum has expertise in commercial banking, team leadership, and client service. Throughout his career, he has helped businesses and individuals achieve their financial goals by delivering personalized guidance and building long-term relationships.


Prior to joining Hancock Whitney, Rosenbaum served as a commercial relationship manager at Mississippi based regional community bank and held a vice president role in commercial banking at a large national bank. He also spent more than three years as chief financial officer of 4QTRS Holdings LLC, a public safety software company based in Vicksburg. Earlier in his career, he spent nearly 12 years at a Mississippi office of a Birmingham, Alabama, based bank, progressing from branch manager to business banker. He began his banking career as a loan officer at the former Union Planters Bank.


Rosenbaum earned a Bachelor of Business Administration in business administration and management from Mississippi State University and a Master of Business Administration in business/commerce from Delta State University. He holds the Certified Treasury Professional designation and Series 6 and 63 licenses.


Actively involved in the community, Rosenbaum coaches little league baseball and soccer and volunteers with Mustard Seed, a Mississippi based nonprofit serving adults with developmental disabilities, reflecting his commitment to helping strengthen the communities Hancock Whitney serves.


##### **About Hancock Whitney**


Since the late 1800s, Hancock Whitney has embodied core values of Honor & Integrity, Strength & Stability, and Commitment to Service, Teamwork, and Personal Responsibility. Hancock Whitney offices and financial centers in Mississippi, Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, and Texas offer comprehensive financial products and services, including traditional and online banking; commercial and small business banking; private banking; trust and investment services; healthcare banking; and mortgage services. The company also operates combined loan and deposit production offices in the greater metropolitan areas of Nashville, Tennessee, and Atlanta, Georgia. More information is available at www.hancockwhitney.com.
